l.i: Antidium V. C. Vicarium. Paschalis laetitiae dies ne illa quidem tenere finit ingenia,
qua flagitia fecerunt: pateat infuetis horridus carcer aliquando luminibus. Alienum
autem censemus ab indulgentia, qui nefariam criminum conscientiam in maiestatem
superbe animauerit, qui parricidali furore raptus, sanguine proprio manum tinxit, qui
cuiusque praeterea hominis caede maculatus est, qui genialis tori ac lectuli fuit inuasor
alieni, qui verecundiae virginalis raptor extitit, qui venerandum cognati sanguinis
vinculum profano caecus violauit incestu, vel qui noxiis quaesita graminibus & diris
immurmurata secretis, mentis & corporis venena composuit: aut qui sacri oris imita-
tor & diuinorum vultuum adpetitor, venerabiles formas sacrilegio eruditus impressit.

page.notes: The text is set as one continuous block with no visible indents, so I have kept it as a single paragraph; the printed paragraph divisions are uncertain. Italic and roman passages were distinguished by eye and may be imperfect, especially at the start of the Lex VII and Lex VIII citations. "Recitatae" and "Lecta" may be italic. Letters read as "infuetis" and "finit" are as printed, with no correction. Printed "Refcribendum" was copied as "Rescribendum" (long s). Catchword "tatis" is at the right foot.
